translated_messages: Calculated power is {power}%; consider a larger sample or longer follow-up to reach the planning target.
Only {events} comparison-effective events are expected; asymptotic power can be unreliable with sparse events. Confirm the design using an appropriate simulation.
The comparison has {events} expected effective events; check the accuracy of the asymptotic approximation.

This is an individual-level survival calculation inflated by 1 + (cluster size - 1) times ICC, not a validated cluster survival design. Planned allocation: {control} control and {treatment} treatment clusters of {size} subjects. Confirm the design with a cluster-specific method.
Fewer than 10 clusters per arm are planned; the simple design-effect approximation does not account for small-cluster degrees of freedom. Obtain a cluster-specific power calculation.
Sensitivity analysis is available for sample-size and power calculations. Select one of those modes to evaluate numerical scenarios.
The assumed HR is below the NI margin; calculated power is {power}%.
The design targets {power}% power to exclude the NI margin at this assumed HR.
The margin requires disease-specific justification from historical evidence and clinical relevance.
A matching superiority comparison cannot be estimated for these assumptions.
At HR 1 there is no superiority effect; a matching superiority event requirement is not defined.
A matching superiority comparison cannot be estimated for these assumptions.
Requires {percent}% of the events a superiority trial at HR {hr} would need
Sequential Multi-arm Family Power Not Available
Per-comparison sequential power is reported. Total study power requires a validated joint arm-and-look calculation and is not estimated here.
The joint normal integration did not meet its accuracy requirement. Per-comparison results remain available.

Control arm: {control} subjects, shared by {comparisons} comparisons; {experimental} per experimental arm. Power is per comparison at the adjusted alpha. For fixed designs, total study power is a joint normal approximation to the probability that at least one comparison rejects when every experimental arm has HR {hr}. Superiority uses both rejection tails; non-inferiority uses one tail. Shared-control correlation uses allocation proportions for Schoenfeld tests and expected-event variances for Cox. This family estimate is unavailable for sequential designs.
The design aims to rule out a hazard ratio of {margin} or worse, assuming a true hazard ratio of {hr}, with {n} subjects and {power}% power at a {alpha}% significance level (one-sided).
The design aims to detect a hazard ratio of {hr} with {n} subjects and {power}% power at a {alpha}% significance level (two-sided).
A {test} power analysis indicates that {n} subjects are required, with {accrual} months of accrual and {followup} months of additional follow-up.
A {test} power analysis for {n} subjects gives {power}% calculated power, with {accrual} months of accrual and {followup} months of additional follow-up.
A {test} power analysis for {n} subjects gives a maximum true HR of {hr} meeting the non-inferiority power target, with {accrual} months of accrual and {followup} months of additional follow-up.
A {test} power analysis for {n} subjects gives a detectable HR of {hr}, with {accrual} months of accrual and {followup} months of additional follow-up.
A {test} power analysis for {n} subjects requires {duration} months in total: {accrual} months of accrual and {followup} months of additional follow-up.
